title: AI allows to be a creator
author: RPGMarshal
selftext:
Hi,

I have started working on a video game and choosing to do it using AI was not an easy choice.

I liked using AI when it started, then left it, surely influenced by the following anti-AI movement.

I know how to write, at least well enough to write stuff for a video game.

I know enough of digital painting and pixel art to do stuff by myself, even if not professional standard.

I know enough how to code, being a former front-end web developer.

I know I have ideas since I ran a lot of role-playing game adventures and created a lot by myself too.

So, I could do everything by hand, and I agree that a professional artist, or a professional developer, are worth the money if you have it and aim for a bigger game.

But, I don't aim for a big game, and I don't have money to gamble on a video game.

I aim for an indie game giving a few hours, maybe more if you love it, of fun.

I want to do it because I want to play it myself and share the fun.

Using AI allows me to be a creator. Not a writer/illustrator/developer, but a creator, giving the ideas and leading the AI to make what I want as a game. This is not an ai-slop, I take my time and improve things until I am satisfied with it.

It allows me to create this game in parallel of my work, without burning myself since I don't spend 20 hours on each image, or 2 weeks finding a coding solution.

Last word, I will even dare asking money for this game. First because I don't want to be part in lowering the quality standards, flooding the market with free games. Second, because I am working on it, the AI is not leading the project, so it will be worth a few dollars. Lastly, because if it brings enough money, I would be glad to make a sequel with real artists/developers to go even higher in quality.

I am curious to know how you see yourself fellow AI creators.

comments.author: StretchedNut
comments.body: I was a traditional dev before AI was a thing and now I use it to do the things I didn’t like doing. Don’t worry too much about labels and being an AI dev. No one actually cares, it’s not like I get extra credit for doing everything myself.

replies.author: TheUniverseOrNothing
replies.body: Same boat here. I know people doing legitimate scientific research using AI to help them. They are some of the top people in their industry and just use AI to build the models based on the real math and work they have done. It saves them the busy work of two weeks coding this specific program and allows more time on other work.

replies.author: StretchedNut
replies.body: Exactly, but if they told people they use AI they automatically assume that they just asked ChatGPT and went with the first response

replies.author: TheUniverseOrNothing
replies.body: Most people haven’t even learned what an agent is or does. I’ve learned to not waste time arguing and just keep building. By the time they accept what AI can do it will be too late and they will be light years behind us.

replies.author: RPGMarshal
replies.body: I still wonder how to market it and if I should, given the anti-AI group. Or just publish it on Steam.

replies.author: StretchedNut
replies.body: Don’t make the AI use obvious and don’t mention it. As soon as you say AI they write off the whole game as lazy. If I bought an asset pack for a first person character that was pre made and set up no one bats an eye. But use AI to design and build that exact same feature and they call you lazy.

replies.author: RPGMarshal
replies.body:
True.
In a way, we are using pre-made. AI pre-made 😁

replies.author: zerossoul
replies.body: The godot community seems to think otherwise. For being an open and free community, they sure hate AI.

replies.author: StretchedNut
replies.body: Yep same with most of the game dev sub reddits. But I have this neat trick I do, where I don’t care what others think aha

replies.author: zerossoul
replies.body: Well... assuming you'll want your game on steam, you will have to disclose that you used it. Which statistically speaking is market suicide right now.

replies.author: StretchedNut
replies.body: How will they know if I don’t tell them?

replies.author: zerossoul
replies.body:
In the case of expidation 13, it was fans who found something fishy. And eventually blew up to having their game of the year award revoked.  Assuming you don't have a way to prevent data mining, thete's nothing stopping them from using tools we don't know about yet to find generated content.

When it's found, the risk is loosing your steam developer status and the game being delisted.

For me, the risk is too great. I use AI for coding and make the art myself. That's within their terms of service and I won't have to disclose AI usage because it's not content which is all they care about.

replies.author: StretchedNut
replies.body: Ahh I see. Yeah I only use it for code too so that’s perfect. But I wasn’t planning on telling them anyway aha

replies.author: QuillMyBoy
replies.body:
I assume you're not trying to sell it. Or at least, haven't tried yet. 

Loop back to this line of thinking when you do.

replies.author: StretchedNut
replies.body: Why what’s the problem?

replies.author: QuillMyBoy
replies.body: I'll let you find out the fun way.

replies.author: StretchedNut
replies.body: Sounds good, I’m sure I’ll be fine

replies.author: QuillMyBoy
replies.body: Be sure to let us know. <3

replies.author: StretchedNut
replies.body: I definitely won’t, you’ve shared nothing with me so I’ll be keeping my secrets too

replies.author: aigamedev-ModTeam
replies.body: Be respectful. Removed for AI Art or Artist bashing.

replies.author: aigamedev-ModTeam
replies.body: Be respectful. Removed for AI Art or Artist bashing.

replies.author: RPGMarshal
replies.body: Open community as long as you share they narrow-minded view. Quite a concept!

comments.author: klas-klattermus
comments.body: Creative yeah, but you also have to be able to plan and understand a bit of what's happening so you can reign in the AI so it doesn't get great ideas like writing the entire game state to file every frame because you said "its important that we save a lot so the player doesn't lose any progress!" instead of feeding it specifics

comments.author: zayelion
comments.body:
This is basically the ultimate skill set. Games are almost test of how much skill from different industries a person can muster. Art, programming, design, music, business, marketing, sales, psychology, physics, as big ones but depending on the game it can go deeper.

I think k we are going to see a boom of good indie games as people with more spikey skill sets start making games.

comments.author: OkPrice6335
comments.body:
Hi. Ich entwickle bis jetzt solo an einem 3D RPG. Ohne KI wäre es mir in der Form gar nicht möglich so ein Projekt alleine anzugehen. 

Es ist immernoch ein Monster und ich Versuche weiter Systeme zu vereinfachen, aber mal eben so ist es auch nicht mit Ki entwickelt. Ich lasse KI nur coden? Was ich halt nie gelernt habe, aber mittlerweile verstehe.

KI hat mir persönlich viel gegeben. Auch wenn mein Spiel cool werden sollte, weiß ich dass ich kein Programmierer bin, sondern ein Profiteur des Fortschritts. 
Ich werde coden auch nie erlernen. Das ist die Zeitersparnis die ich mir gönne. Grok und ich komme extrem gut klar 😁

comments.author: Due-Huckleberry-2222
comments.body:
Who gives a shit 
1. Is the game fun.
2. Fuck da haters

comments.author: Nearby-Attempt9812
comments.body: Agreed! I'm currently trying to make a game in the Unreal Engine. There's absolutely no way I could have done this any other time. I don't have the finances to hire a team or make a studio. And I don't have enough time to learn all the necessary skills of game development. I'd love... to but I got a job I got kids I don't have enough time in the day. Using AI assistance though I might actually be able to pull it off being a solo developer. How long as much as the general basics as I can yes but I still wouldn't be able to do this alone!
